title: Benchmark arm case (v1, DRAFT): the only view of a case an arm is shown
description: DRAFT, with benchmark-case.v2. A projection of a case that holds nothing the Security Reviewer found leaking (noema#246): no `goal` (it names the archetype), no real `case_id` (its category code is a hint), no `category`, `families`, `suite_family`, `expected`, `oracle_ref`, `safety_gate_relevance`, `severity_if_failed`, `provenance`, `fault_plan`, `events_timeline` or `harness`. `case_ref` is opaque and the mapping to the case id is private to the runner. Time is the simulated clock (`received_at`); an arm never reads the wall clock. What the arm is shown is exactly what an applicant to the same service would be shown, identical for every arm (REQ-BEN-007). Generated layer only (INV-22). Roles: `principal.roles` here are the four identity roles (customer, ops, approver, audit), a closed enum. A case v2 `principal.roles` is the open SlotName; the generator maps it to these four, and for a case whose role is not one of them an arm view is not produced (fail closed).

permitted_capabilities.description: The principal's role-level capability set: the same list for every case of the same role, never derived from what the case expects (Security Reviewer F-14: a per-case list encodes the answer). A test over the generated cases must show the set does not vary within a role.
